question: Does remote work increase or decrease employee productivity?

starFinding.text: Remote work neither uniformly increases nor decreases productivity; its effect depends systematically on job type, organizational infrastructure, temporal factors, work-arrangement model, and individual differences.
starFinding.sourceQuote: Remote work productivity effects are not uniformly positive or negative but depend systematically on job characteristics, organizational infrastructure, temporal factors, work arrangement models, and individual differences.

top3.text: Remote work can enhance productivity through increased flexibility, autonomy, and reduced commuting time, but its impact depends on both individual and organizational factors rather than work location alone.
top3.sourceQuote: The findings indicate that remote work can enhance productivity through increased flexibility, autonomy, and reduced commuting time.

top3.text: In a digital-era study, 65% of respondents experienced an increase in productivity while working remotely, implying the remaining 35% saw no gain or a decrease.
top3.sourceQuote: 65% of respondents experienced an increase in productivity while working remotely

top3.text: Productivity increased or held steady for many knowledge workers in creative, IT, and consultancy roles, while roles requiring close teamwork or physical presence suffered and long-term remote work risked performance fatigue.
top3.sourceQuote: Productivity has either increased or stayed the same for a large number of knowledge workers.

doNotPromote: The single early-pandemic literature review (Dr. G. Udayasuriyan, abstract-only) reporting an overall decline in productivity attributed to working from home — a lone, context-limited null/negative result that must not be ranked #1 as the answer.

The isolated bivariate claim that remote work is positively correlated with performance so 'as remote work increases, employee performance also increases' — an over-simplified single-study correlation that must not be promoted as the headline answer over the context-dependent synthesis.
